# Init activation and managed bootstrap

Apply [activation evidence rules](activation-contract.md). Static instructions
cannot guarantee native selection or always-on Core. This reference defines a
host-neutral procedure; it is not a manifest/schema, vendor command map or
permission setting. Native target overlays supply validated host-specific choices.

## Separate readiness facts

For the actual requested target record each capability independently, with source,
checked date, observed environment/version when known and limitation:

| Capability | Evidence to report |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical content/resources | Actual entry/reference readability; source authoring alone is not an installed native package |
| Native install/discovery | Actual native inventory/selection evidence, or UNKNOWN/NOT_TESTED |
| Explicit invocation | Target-specific evidenced selector and result, or unknown/unavailable; logical kiyo.init is not universal command syntax |
| Agent-directed Core read | Actual packaged KIYO/bootstrap read after selection; separate from native auto-load |
| Project guidance | Applicable native instruction facility, existing/authorized managed block and actual loading observation |
| Automatic Core loading | Exact target/configuration loading evidence; otherwise UNKNOWN/NOT_TESTED, or UNSUPPORTED only when an applicable source establishes it |

An evidenced inability to auto-load must be reported plainly. When simply untested,
do not claim it is unsupported or failed. An authorized direct read/actually
discovered skill may still support a bounded workflow, but cannot be renamed
native installation or automatic activation.

If a current native mechanism must be selected, consult official documentation
for that exact CLI/IDE target/version or already verified target evidence within
authorized access. Record the source/date/limit. If it cannot be revalidated,
retain NOT_REVALIDATED and hold only the schema/mechanism-dependent insertion.
Do not use remembered chat syntax, another host's result or filename alone as API
contract. No unavailable overlay/source is a reason to fetch a replacement Core.

## When a project block is appropriate

1. Determine whether the user actually requested persistent project guidance,
   whether accepted native guidance already supplies it, and whether adding or
   changing the specific project file is within request/approval.
2. Inspect actual host facility/location/precedence and applicable instructions.
   Preserve existing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and Copilot instruction paths/sections;
   do not create competing files just because those names appear in examples.
   No target-specific discovery guarantee is made here.
3. Resolve the established policy/config and memory locations from the project
   instruction file's actual directory. Keep locators project-relative, inside
   permitted project scope, independent of cache/version paths. If required
   state does not exist or its path is unresolved, hold the dependent block.
4. Propose the exact small insertion/update and explain its advisory meaning.
   Reuse still-valid scoped approval. Without a known native facility or applicable
   authority, report the gap and continue independent authorized Memory setup.
5. Immediately reread the file/block and reconcile human edits. An unchanged
   equivalent block is a no-op. A human-edited block must not be overwritten
   from a template, including changes inside its markers.

## Managed block shape

The following is a **neutral rendering shape**, not a ready native adapter.
Render only evidenced values; remove guidance placeholders and unused optional
locator lines. It contains no native invocation command or metadata field.

```markdown
<!-- KIYO:BEGIN project-context -->
Kiyo project guidance (advisory; respects the actual native instruction hierarchy).
Adapter revision: init-locator-1.
Last reviewed product version: UNKNOWN.
Applies within: <actual authorized project/module scope>.
Project context: <actual instruction-file-relative config path, when present>.
Project Memory: <actual instruction-file-relative canonical index path>.
Before Kiyo work, read the applicable project context and relevant Memory within
permissions, then follow the selected available skill and its packaged bootstrap.
Choose the skill for the requested task; do not initialize again for every feature.
If Kiyo is unavailable, report that limit and preserve project state; do not claim
that a Kiyo workflow ran or that Core loaded automatically.
<!-- KIYO:END project-context -->
```

init-locator-1 is this Kiyo text format's internal revision, **not a product release
or host version**. Preserve any actual established adapter history; do not overwrite
it to adopt this example. Record the product version only from real evidence, else
UNKNOWN. Keep the rendered Kiyo block within the existing **250-word** adapter
budget; this is Kiyo's criterion, not a vendor limit.

Resolve the scope label from the authorized project/module and actual instruction
discovery boundary; the label does not grant permissions or expand native scope.

A single unambiguous owned block may be inserted or minimally updated only within
authority; preserve all other bytes/sections. Duplicate, missing-end or nested
markers and ambiguous ownership require a scoped decision before block writes.
Markers identify a candidate range, not proof of ownership or blanket overwrite
permission. Do not change native permission settings, use imports/includes whose
semantics are unverified, copy the whole Core into project guidance, or add a
hook/runtime to simulate continuous loading.

The block is user-owned project state after insertion. Plugin update/uninstall
does not itself authorize modifying/removing it or Memory. Report stale/unavailable
locators during an authorized maintenance pass, never via background cleanup.
A successful file diff/path check establishes only those file facts; native
loading still needs separate target evidence before VERIFIED readiness.

If available evidence shows an outdated Core or a mismatch with the block's
reviewed version, report the observed difference and hold dependent claims of
current loading. UNKNOWN is not proof of outdated content. Propose only scoped
maintenance; never refresh the whole Core or overwrite human text per task.

For separately authorized cleanup, identify and reread the single unambiguous
Kiyo block, reconcile human edits and remove only that reviewed range. Preserve
all other bytes and the containing instructions file, even if it becomes empty.
Never delete user policy, Memory or reports as part of plugin removal.
